Read all five proof steps, the complete slope-selection algorithm and its well-definedness proof, and all nine supplier statements. C^3 and compactness give uniform M1,M2,M3; IVT fixes the sign of f' and MVT gives same-sign secants with magnitude at least c. Degree-two Taylor at an interior node gives d_minus=s-hq/2+O(h^2), d_plus=s+hq/2+O(h^2), with node-independent bounds. Reciprocal expansion cancels first-order terms, and |s|<=M1 with M1>=c>0 keeps the harmonic denominator uniformly away from zero. The endpoint formula (3d0-d1)/2 cancels the first-order term; for small h the clip is inactive and same-sign secants exclude the cap. Reflection covers the right endpoint, including N=2. The reader correctly states a<b, integer N>=2 and h=(b-a)/N>0: without a<b, a=b makes all secant divisions undefined. Fritsch–Butland pp. 301–302 give the uniform-grid harmonic rule and second-order derivative context; the complete estimate is established locally. No AC. Read all four proof steps and eleven actual supplier statements/proofs as needed. The fixed positive-width grid satisfies the reviewed slope lemma. C^3 suffices: degree-two Taylor gives |r(x)|<=Mh^3/6 throughout each cell, and Taylor for f' gives |r'(right)|<=Mh^2/2. Hermite linearity and polynomial reproduction imply |H-f|<=5Mh^3/6; slope errors contribute at most 2Cs h^3. These bounds and their thresholds are independent of i and N. Continuity of |P_h-f| on nonempty compact [a,b] justifies the attained maximum. The residual-bound omission is immediate nonfatal polish; grid admissibility is the substantive missing hypothesis. Read all three verification steps and all six cited suppliers. For n>=2 the fixed grid [-1,1], h=1/n contains -2h,-h,0,h,2h, with -h and 0 interior even for n=2. Four local secants are (-3h,-h,h,3h); the harmonic rule gives m(-h)=-3h/2 and the opposite-sign branch gives m(0)=0. The Hermite formula gives error h^2 t(1-t)^2/2, hence 2h^2/27 at t=1/3. Continuity and nonempty compactness justify the local maximum; a uniform Ch^3 bound implies 2/27<=C/n, impossible. f'(0)=0, so the earlier nonstationary theorem is not misapplied. The reader replaces the shrinking five-node interval by grids on one fixed domain, closing the nonfatal witness-quantifier gap in the original comparison with a theorem whose constants depend on [a,b]; the original local computation was already correct. No outside item consumes this example, no substantial prerequisite is missing, and no AC is used.
